name: An Ann Arbor lot

place_source.title: Wikidata: Ann Arbor (Q485172), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A suburban lot under Ann Arbor's maples and oaks: a lawn, an oak and hickory at the back for jays and squirrels, a redbud and dogwood border, white-cedar, hemlock and yew that stay green all winter, and a rain garden that draws toads, garter snakes and raccoons after dark.

facts.text: Ann Arbor has a typically Midwestern humid continental climate (Köppen Dfa), which is influenced by the Great Lakes.

source.title: Wikipedia: Ann Arbor, Michigan
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Ann Arbor, Michigan", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Ann Arbor is nicknamed "Tree Town", both because of its name and because of the dense forestation of its parks and residential areas: the city contains more than 50,000 trees along its streets and an equal number in parks.

source.title: Wikipedia: Ann Arbor, Michigan
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Ann Arbor, Michigan", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The city contains over 160 municipal parks, ranging from small neighbourhood green spots to large recreation areas.

source.title: Wikipedia: Ann Arbor, Michigan
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Ann Arbor, Michigan", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Into the early 2000s the emerald ash borer had destroyed many of the city's approximately 10,500 ash trees.

source.title: Wikipedia: Ann Arbor, Michigan
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Ann Arbor, Michigan", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The city's municipal airport lies at an elevation of 839 feet (256 m), while the terrain rises to 1,015 feet (309 m) on the city's west side.

source.title: Wikipedia: Ann Arbor, Michigan
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Ann Arbor, Michigan", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The red-bellied woodpecker is a major predator of the invasive emerald ash borer in the US Midwest, removing up to 85 percent of borer larvae in a single infested ash tree.

source.title: Wikipedia: Red-bellied woodpecker
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Red-bellied woodpecker", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Eastern fox squirrels tolerate human proximity and thrive in crowded urban and suburban environments, nesting in an attic as happily as in a hollow tree.

source.title: Wikipedia: Fox squirrel
